name: Calculus 3: many variables
description: Vectors in space, functions of several variables, multiple integrals, vector fields and the great theorems, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Calculus 3 realm ("Calculus 3: many variables"): space, vectors, functions of several variables, multiple integrals,
vector fields and the theorems that link a boundary to its inside, for an adult who has finished Foundations, Calculus 1
and Calculus 2. Same Kepler outpost, now working in three dimensions, and Mira is still the mentor. The concept plan is
docs/plans/CALC3-PLAN.md.

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Nothing here lies flat any more, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have the derivatives and integrals from Calculus 1 and 2. I’ll go through the worked example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
Everything here has three directions.
Learn to measure in all of them.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome back. The outpost is climbing off the ground: docks overhead, wind across the plain, air moving through every dome. We begin with the plainest thing in space, two survey beacons and the distance between them.
copy.allDone: You did it. You can map, climb, fill and ventilate anything at the outpost, in every direction at once. Differential equations come next, where the outpost’s machines start answering back.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from points in space to the great theorems. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the result before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Many variables, measured.
help.intro: Calculus 3 starts again from the beginning in space: points, vectors and the two ways to multiply them. It then adds lines and planes, functions of several variables, gradients, multiple integrals, vector fields and the theorems that link a boundary to its inside. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: A vector is typed as its components in separate boxes, never as a formula; angles are in radians and lengths in metres, and a volume with π asks for k in k·π.
